title: Κίχλα
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 157 (= Perry 86). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἔν τινι μυρσινῶνι κίχλα ἐνέμετο· διὰ δὲ τὴν γλυκύτητα τοῦ καρποῦ οὐκ ἀφίστατο.
sentences.tr: En tini myrsinōni kichla enemeto· dia de tēn glykytēta tou karpou ouk aphistato.
sentences.l: In a certain myrtle-grove a thrush was feeding; and because of the sweetness of the fruit she would not withdraw.
sentences.n: A μυρσινών is a plantation of myrtle, whose small dark berries are the fruit meant. ἀφίστατο is the imperfect middle of ἀφίστημι, "stand off, withdraw" — the imperfect of a refusal kept up, "she would not go away". Chambry's ano teleia (·) is a stop lighter than a full stop and heavier than a comma.

sentences.t: Ἰξευτὴς δὲ παρατηρησάμενος ἐμφιλοχωροῦσαν ἰξεύσας συνέλαβε.
sentences.tr: Ixeutēs de paratērēsamenos emphilochōrousan ixeusas synelabe.
sentences.l: But a fowler, having watched her keeping fondly to the spot, and having spread his birdlime, caught her.
sentences.i: But a fowler marked how she clung to the place, spread his lime, and took her.
sentences.n: ἰξός is birdlime, smeared on twigs; ἰξεύω is to hunt with it, and the ἰξευτής is the man whose trade that is. ἐμφιλοχωροῦσαν is a supplementary participle after παρατηρησάμενος: he watched her as she lingered.

sentences.t: Καὶ δὴ μέλλουσα ἀναιρεῖσθαι ἔφη· « Δειλαία εἰμί, ἥτις διὰ τροφῆς γλυκύτητα σωτηρίας στερίσκομαι. »
sentences.tr: Kai dē mellousa anaireisthai ephē· « Deilaia eimi, hētis dia trophēs glykytēta sōtērias steriskomai. »
sentences.l: And indeed, being about to be killed, she said: « Wretched am I, who because of the sweetness of food am robbed of my life. »
sentences.i: And as she was about to be killed she said: « Unhappy creature that I am, to be robbed of my life for the sweetness of a meal. »
sentences.n: μέλλω with the present infinitive is "to be on the point of"; ἀναιρέω in the passive is the plain word for being made away with. ἥτις, the indefinite relative, gives the ground: "seeing that I…". στερίσκομαι takes the genitive of what is lost, and σωτηρία here is life itself.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος πρὸς ἄνδρα ἄσωτον δι’ ἡδυπάθειαν ἀπολωλότα εὔκαιρός ἐστιν.
sentences.tr: Ho logos pros andra asōton di’ hēdypatheian apolōlota eukairos estin.
sentences.l: Against a profligate man ruined through love of pleasure the story is well-timed.
sentences.n: πρός with the accusative in this formula is hostile: the story is aimed at such a man. ἄσωτος is the spendthrift, literally the man past saving. ἀπολωλότα is the second perfect participle of ἀπόλλυμι, which in that tense is intransitive: "having come to ruin".
